arch_per_nbcWC.new_text: RULE: National Building Code of Canada 2020, Div. B 3.7.2 (repo copy nbc.txt; BCBC 2024, NBC(AE) 2023 and VBBL 2025 compared word by word in bcbc2024.txt, nbc_ab2023.txt, vbbl2025_v1.txt): 3.7.2.1.(2) industrial occupant load for washrooms 'permitted to be based solely on the total number of staff for which the floor area is designed, where the floor area is only intermittently occupied or where the presence of occupants is transitory' (Note A-3.7.2.1.(2): 'Substations and parking garages are examples'); 3.7.2.2.(2) both sexes may share a single water closet if occupant load 'not more than 10' (VBBL: 'not more than 25'); Table 3.7.2.2.-C industrial, per sex: 1-10 persons 1 WC, 11-25 2, 26-50 3, 51-75 4, 76-100 5, over 100 6 plus 1 per 30; Table 3.7.2.2.-B business and personal services: 1-25 1, 26-50 2, over 50 3 plus 1 per 50; 3.7.2.3.(1) at least one lavatory per room with 1 or 2 WCs. NBC(AE) only: 3.7.2.1.(6) 'plumbing fixtures are not required for a building of low human occupancy' (Note: 'pump houses, equipment storage shacks'). BCBC and VBBL 3.8.2.8.(4): where WCs are required, 'at least one universal washroom shall be provided in the entrance storey' unless an accessible path leads to one elsewhere (NBC and NBC(AE) 3.8.2.8.(4): 'at least one barrier-free water closet'). VBBL 3.7.2.2.(15): two unisex toilet rooms may serve an industrial or business occupancy if suite ≤200 m² and occupant load ≤60. VBBL 3.7.2.9.(1): occupant load over 200 needs at least one gender-neutral washroom facility. No code clause requires a break room or lunchroom (our reading of NBC Part 3). ‖ CHECK 2 (1 Nov 2026, fixed): all clauses confirmed; 3.8.2.8.(4) is in VBBL too (NBC/AB wording is barrier-free WC); VBBL 3.7.2.2.(15) added.

arch_per_gcpsg009hvm.new_text: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-009 (2022) Security Fencing Considerations Guide, effective 2022-01-27, approved 2022-03-16, page modified 2025-11-03 (official RCMP page; supplements register rcmpGCPSG009 and arch_sec2_gcpsg009b): 8.2 ASTM F2656 'details the requirements for the Hostile Vehicle Mitigation measures'; M30 (K4) 30 mph, M40 (K8) 40 mph, M50 (K12) 50 mph, 15,000 lb vehicle; P1 <1 m, P2 1.1-7 m, P3 7-30 m, P4 ≥30.1 m penetration; 'there is no limit to how far the vehicle can travel past the barrier to be certified'; protection depends on 'the setback and standoff distances' set by a TRA. 9.1 bollards, large planters or rocks as 'larger, more robust vehicular security barriers' where pedestrian traffic is high; back-filled retaining wall as a vehicle barrier; 'Blast pressure falls off with increased standoff'. 9.1, 9.5 ditches and berms. 10.3.2 fences with 'integral crash beams or cables'. 10.6 gate barriers: fixed or movable bollards, wedge/ramp barriers, locking arms, cable barriers; 'the first choice to protect a gate is to limit the approach speed of a vehicle' (curves, chicanes, parallel approach); halving speed cuts impact force to a quarter; gates latch 'approximately every four feet of vertical height'. 10.1 minimum security fence 2.4 m, high security ≥3.6 m. 5 and 9.4: provincial or municipal laws and AHJ height limits may restrict fences. No bollard spacing. — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-009-2022-security-fencing-considerations-guide ‖ CHECK 2 (1 Nov 2026, fixed): 10.5 does not contain 'integral crash beams or cables'; cited 10.3.2 only.
